more.title: Scientists identify avian cholera as major cause of penguin deaths in Antarctica
more.summary: Thousands of Adélie penguins found dead in Antarctica in 2024 were primarily victims of avian cholera, not high pathogenicity avian influenza (H5N1) as researchers initially suspected, according to a study published today in Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences.

more.title: A trip to Mars could come at a heartbreaking cost
more.summary: When astronauts first travel to Mars or anywhere else in deep space, they will have to contend with two problems that our planet protects us from on its surface—radiation and weightlessness. Scientists already know both can have a profound impact on the human body, but the extent of that impact and how long it can last remain a mystery.

more.summary: In this Crunchbase News exclusive, we spoke to Marklo AI founder Jessica Herrin about her solution to the marketing problems she encountered when building earlier startups, and how a group of investors, led by Forerunner, are backing that early experience with a $5 million seed funding round.

more.title: Scimplify raises $25M to challenge China’s grip on critical materials with AI
more.author: Jagmeet Singh
more.summary: Scimplify's annualized revenue run rate has tripled to $200 million as it eyes U.S. expansion.

more.title: Now you see them: Researchers uncover patterns in vessels that vanish at sea
more.summary: Across the waters of West Africa, commercial fishing vessels vanish along international boundary lines.

more.title: Scientists alarmed as super El Niño collides with 'strange uptick' in Galapagos iguana trafficking
more.summary: The only lizard in the world that can live and forage at sea may now be in a fight for survival. International scientists warn black-market trafficking of Galapagos marine iguanas is peaking just as the super El Niño decimates their natural food source.

more.title: Floqer’s AI agents research sales prospects so teams don’t have to
more.author: Lauren Forristal
more.summary: The problem Floqer is trying to solve is familiar to anyone who has worked in sales or revenue operations.

more.title: Climate adaptation's delivery gap: Turning national plans into action
more.summary: By 2025, 143 of 154 developing countries had a National Adaptation Plan process in place, yet implementation has not kept pace. Many countries still lack the institutional capacity, project preparation and finance needed to turn their priorities into strategies, bankable projects and results on the ground.

more.title: Social service agencies need safeguards when using AI
more.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used by social service agencies to handle cases involving child abuse, intimate partner violence and elder abuse. But a University of Iowa researcher and former social worker says the agencies need to establish safeguards to ensure that AI technology does not lead to bias against vulnerable or disadvantaged populations.

more.title: Nepal flood triggered by rock and ice avalanche: Report
more.summary: Nepal's disaster authority said Wednesday that an avalanche of rock and ice triggered a recent flash flood, echoing the mountain collapse that unleashed a tsunami-like wall of water in August.

more.title: Can AI feel safer than human advice for consumers who face discrimination?
more.summary: What should you cook for dinner on a budget of 20 euros when you have a guest with a gluten intolerance? A shopper might ask a shop assistant for advice or consult, for example, Hopla, the AI-powered shopping assistant launched by French supermarket chain Carrefour. Behind this everyday choice lies a broader question: when faced with a recommendation, who do we trust more? A human being or an AI?

more.title: Scientists reveal why some workout recovery tricks can backfire
more.summary: Ice baths, massages, compression garments, and recovery supplements promise faster muscle recovery, but research suggests their benefits are often overstated, and some techniques may even undermine long-term gains. Scientists say the most effective recovery methods are far simpler and cheaper: getting enough sleep, eating well, and giving muscles time to rebuild.

more.title: Meet the five companies competing in the Startup Battlefield finals at Disrupt 2026
more.author: Anthony Ha
more.summary: It’s time to unveil the five companies that will be competing in the Startup Battlefield finals.

more.title: Cornell scientists identify rare human genetic disorder in two unusually long-legged cats
more.summary: Two unusually long-legged cats have helped scientists uncover the first genetically confirmed cases of Marfan syndrome in domestic felines. Researchers at Cornell University discovered that the brothers carried two altered copies of a gene linked to the rare connective tissue disorder, which can affect the eyes, heart, and blood vessels.

more.title: The secret to easier exercise as an adult may start in childhood
more.summary: Exercise during childhood could have a surprising lifelong benefit, potentially making physical activity less exhausting in adulthood. In a study involving guinea fowl, researchers discovered that birds accustomed to carrying weights while growing up could carry those weights as adults without using extra energy, while untrained birds burned 23% more.

more.title: Fair climate transitions need more than financial support, evidence review suggests
more.summary: The transition to a low-carbon economy will not affect all people and places equally. Although its overall benefits may outweigh its costs, workers may lose jobs, households may face higher prices and communities dependent on carbon-intensive industries may experience lasting economic and social disruption.

more.title: Green, pink and purple: Astronomers reveal the surprising true colors of white dwarf stars
more.summary: University of Warwick astronomers have shown that white dwarf stars can glow in a range of colors, including the first star ever found that would appear green to the human eye.
